experimental_method: Flow saturation method: compressed gas bubbled through two water-containing cells in series at constant T, expanded to about 1 atm, water collected on weighed magnesium perchlorate drying tubes and gas volume measured with a wet-test meter.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature controlled to +/-0.01 C, measured to +/-0.02 C; pressure uncertainty not more than 0.3% at about 20 atm and smaller at higher pressure; water measurements reproducible to +/-0.5%, probably accurate within 1% (slightly larger at lowest concentrations); B12 uncertainty about +/-5 ml/mole.
quality_remarks: Authors report good agreement with Bartlett (N2, 50 C); Saddington and Krase data judged less consistent; Olds, Sage and Lacey CH4 data 4% higher at 50 atm and 71.1 C. Water-weight correction never above 0.2%. Dry-gas purities: N2 <0.2% impurity, Ar <0.002%, CH4 <=100 ppm. Rows are mean values of two or more determinations.
not_extracted_tables: Table II (pure-component second virial coefficients and vapour pressure of water): literature / reference values, not measured here
row_counts: Table I printed data rows 37 (N2 13, Ar 12, CH4 12) plus 3 gas-name label rows; written 37 plus 3 label rows (40 rows after header)

Sanity: pressures increase within each temperature sub-block; y1 decreases with pressure and increases with T as expected; no duplicate rows. Printed T has no explicit temperature scale. Printed column 'y1' denotes water (component 1).
